paras: The threatened lynching of Dave Richardson was a reported plan by a party of white men to storm the county jail at Tallahassee, Florida, on a Saturday night in August 1900, probably August 11, and lynch Richardson, a Black prisoner accused of killing a white farmer named Harmon Gray. Governor Bloxham ordered a local militia company, the Governor's Guards, to protect the jail, and no attack was reported.

The Savannah Morning News described Harmon Gray as "a prominent young white farmer of Leon county." On August 2 the Weekly Tallahasseean reported that "the murderer of Harmon Gray" had been arrested in Georgia, brought back, and placed in the Tallahassee jail. Sheriff Pearce, the paper said, was keeping a close watch on the prisoner until the fall term of the Circuit Court, when it expected him to be convicted and hanged. That item did not name the prisoner or give his race, and the coverage does not say when or how Gray was killed.

According to a report published in the Savannah Morning News on August 14, word reached Tallahassee "from reliable sources" that an "attacking party of whites" would storm the county jail on Saturday night and lynch Richardson. In response, Governor Bloxham ordered the Governor's Guards, described as a Tallahassee military company, to go to the jail and protect the prisoner. The troops remained on guard through the night. The report does not say that any attackers appeared, and no attack on the jail is described.
No report of Richardson's trial or sentence, or of any further threat against him, was found in coverage through the end of September 1900.

The threat appears in the coverage only as a short item headed "Troops Were Ordered Out." in the Savannah Morning News, a Georgia daily. The item stated without qualification that Richardson had "recently killed" Gray and described the would-be lynchers only as an "attacking party of whites," naming none of them. Its emphasis fell on the governor's order and the overnight guard rather than on the mob.

Before the threat, the local Weekly Tallahasseean had likewise headed its item "Gray's Murderer Here" and predicted that the prisoner would "no doubt be convicted" and hanged. No coverage of the episode was found in the Black press.

reader.title: Threatened lynching of Dave Richardson
bases: A party of whites reportedly planned to storm the county jail and lynch a Black prisoner, and troops were called out to prevent it; no attack is reported (A3).

No one was killed: the coverage reports only a threatened mob attack on the jail, which troops guarded overnight (A3). The planned act was an extralegal lynching over an accused killing, but the size of the 'attacking party' is not given (A3).

The threat and the troop deployment appear only in one Savannah Morning News item (A3); the Weekly Tallahasseean item (A1) confirms only that Gray's accused killer was jailed in Tallahassee, before the threat.

accounts.label: Tallahassee report in Savannah daily
accounts.gist: Reliable reports said whites would storm the jail Saturday night and lynch Richardson; the governor sent the Governor's Guards, who stood guard overnight.

accounts.label: Local weekly (before the threat)
accounts.gist: Gray's killer, arrested in Georgia, was held under close watch by Sheriff Pearce awaiting the fall court term and an expected conviction and hanging.

framing.detail: Headed 'Troops Were Ordered Out.', the item centers the governor's order and the guard, calls the would-be lynchers an 'attacking party of whites', and states as fact that Richardson 'recently killed' Gray.
The Weekly Tallahasseean called the prisoner 'Gray's Murderer' and anticipated that he would 'no doubt be convicted' and hanged.

record_check.dossier: An unnamed 'attacking party of whites' (size not stated)
Revenge for the alleged killing of Harmon Gray, a white farmer (implied by the accusation; no mob statement reported)
Inferred from 'Saturday night' in a Tuesday, August 14 report; consistent
The threat itself appears in 1 article; the Weekly Tallahasseean (Aug. 2) adds background on the arrest and custody of Gray's accused killer

info: Saturday night before the Tuesday, August 14, 1900, report; probably August 11, 1900 (inferred from 'Saturday night')
Dave Richardson, described as 'a negro', confined in the county jail; not harmed in any report
Accused of killing Harmon Gray, described as 'a prominent young white farmer of Leon county'; the paper states the killing as fact
Troops remained on guard overnight; no attack reported

sources.note: 'Gray's Murderer Here': the unnamed killer of Harmon Gray, arrested in Georgia, is held in the Tallahassee jail by Sheriff Pearce until the fall Circuit Court term; linked to Richardson only by the victim's name.
quotes: Sheriff Pearce is keeping a close watch on him until the fall term of the Circuit Court, when he will no doubt be convicted

a negro therein confined who recently killed Harmon Gray, a prominent young white farmer of Leon county.
The troops remained on guard during the night.

set_aside: Tallahassee news column; a different man, P. W. Richardson, shot and killed a Black man at a turpentine camp and was acquitted in Wakulla county on self-defense. Not this episode.
